first_impression.reaction: I googled 'getting married in Hawaii' because it's one of three places on our shortlist and I wanted to know if the legal side is a nightmare. The intro answers that in two sentences: apply online, see an agent together, licensed officiant, 30 days, no residency, no blood test. That's what I needed to know before I let myself get attached. No 'say I do in paradise', thank god. It reads like someone has actually stood at the counter in Honolulu. I read the licence and timing sections properly, skimmed the ESTA, climate and permit bits, and would send the timing section to James. What it doesn't do is tell me anything about our guests, which is half of what we're worried about.

journey.quote: Getting married in Hawaii as an Australian couple is straightforward.
journey.reaction: Good. Straight answer up front, then the steps that back it up. As a lawyer I like that it says what the process is rather than promising it's easy.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Hawaii?
journey.quote: The marriage licence is what permits the marriage to take place. The marriage certificate shows that a legal marriage has been performed.
journey.reaction: Useful distinction. I would have mixed those up. This is the 'confidence the legal side is sorted' bit we want.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Keep both passports with you, not in the luggage you send ahead to the villa.
journey.reaction: Small, practical, the kind of thing only someone who has seen it go wrong would say. More of this please.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Australians visiting the United States for less than 90 days may be eligible to apply for an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) and enter under the Visa Waiver Program.
journey.reaction: Fine, but I know about ESTA. What I actually thought about here was our 40-odd overseas guests and my grandparents needing one too. The page only talks to the two of us.

journey.quote: Complete the online marriage licence application at emrs.ehawaii.gov and pay the required fee.
journey.reaction: How much is the fee? It's the one cost on the whole page and it's left blank. It's probably small, but 'the required fee' and later 'a fee applies' for the certificate copies read as vague when everything else is so precise.

journey.section: Step 2: Book your appointment with an agent
journey.quote: If you are marrying on a neighbour island, book an agent there. It saves an inter-island flight in the busiest week of your trip.
journey.reaction: Exactly the insider detail I look for. Shows someone has thought about the actual week, not just the paperwork.

journey.section: Pick up your licence together, in person
journey.quote: If one of you lands a day later than the other, the appointment waits for the second flight.
journey.reaction: James is likely flying in after me from a work trip, so this is real for us. Honest trade-off, said plainly.

journey.quote: Younger applicants need a certified copy of their birth certificate; check with the agent.
journey.reaction: Younger than what? The line before says the legal age is 18. I read it twice and still don't know if 'younger' means under 18 or something else, and whether it affects us.

journey.quote: The licence list does not include a Certificate of No Impediment.
journey.reaction: Helpful because I'd assumed we'd need one. The follow-on about registries and DFAT is a bit of a tangent, but I get the 'just in case'.

journey.section: Timing the appointment around your arrival
journey.quote: For couples flying in from Australia, that means one practical thing: see the agent in Hawaii, in the first days after you land.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I'd forward. Clear action, tied to our itinerary, with the buffer before the welcome dinner. Very good.

journey.quote: Start early, and do not print their name on the order of service until the licence is confirmed.
journey.reaction: Good warning, we'd half thought about asking a friend. But 'start early' is vague. How long does a performer licence take? Weeks? Months?

journey.quote: Processing usually takes up to four to six weeks, and delays can occur.
journey.reaction: Helpful, especially with the 'order more than one copy' tip for name changes and passports. That's admin I'd rather sort once.

journey.section: Registering or recognising your marriage at home
journey.quote: Once Australia recognises your Hawaii marriage, you cannot marry again in Australia.
journey.reaction: The heading says 'Registering' but two paragraphs earlier I was told you cannot register it. The content is really about not marrying twice and having a recommitment lunch at home. The heading made me think I'd missed a step.

journey.section: Permits for beach and outdoor ceremonies
journey.quote: Sand is public in a way a lawn is not.
journey.reaction: Nice line, and the permit detail is the sort of thing nobody tells you. I skimmed the DLNR detail, but I now know to ask the venue who holds the permit.

journey.quote: Day length runs from about 11 hours to about 13.5 hours.
journey.reaction: Skimmed. The leeward-for-sunset point is the useful bit; the water temperature and day-length numbers read like an encyclopaedia.

journey.quote: It suits a wedding weekend built around one resort and a long evening on the terrace.
journey.reaction: Maui gets this kind of 'who it suits' line and it's the most helpful thing in the section. Oahu, Kauai and Hawaii Island mostly get airports and landmarks. I wanted the same 'suits a couple who...' for each, especially which island is easiest for 80 guests and older relatives.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One point of contact and inclusions in writing is what we want. But 'start to finish' is the 'end-to-end' line every planner uses. The Four Seasons Hualalai link is the closest thing to proof, and I'd click it.

journey.quote: Ask your officiant what the ceremony itself requires on the day, including witnesses, and how the marriage is registered afterwards.
journey.reaction: This FAQ doesn't answer its own question. If the honest answer is 'check with your officiant', fine, but it reads like a dodge in a page that's otherwise so direct.

journey.section: Plan your Hawaii wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD quotes and fee in writing directly hit our currency-surprise fear. Calm close, no hard sell. Not enough to enquire on its own.

turn_offs_found.why: The only cost in the process is left unstated (and again as 'a fee applies' for certificate copies). Vague pricing is a turn-off for us, even for a small fee, because it makes me wonder what else isn't spelled out.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim every planner makes. With no Hawaii wedding or detail about who is on the ground nearby, it sits flatter than the very specific advice above it.

would_share_with: James: the 'Timing the appointment around your arrival' section and the 'appointment waits for the second flight' line, because it shapes when we both need to land
My parents: the intro and 'Is a Hawaii marriage recognised in Australia?' FAQ, because Dad will ask whether it's 'properly legal' at home

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-hawaii&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure, and AUD quotes plus fee in writing are the right reassurances. But Hawaii is one of three options, we're 14 months out, and I haven't seen a real Hawaii wedding from them. I'd click the Four Seasons Hualalai guide first and maybe look at the Concierge page, not enquire today.

top_3_changes: Give each island the same 'who it suits' line Maui gets ('It suits a wedding weekend built around one resort...'), ideally framed around guest logistics (flights from Australia, connections through Honolulu, ease for older guests), because choosing an island for 60 to 90 guests is the decision we actually face.

Fix the two small confusions: clarify who 'Younger applicants' refers to given the legal age of 18, and rename 'Registering or recognising your marriage at home' since the page has just said you cannot register it (e.g. 'Celebrating again at home').

Add one short line for guests in the entry section (everyone travelling needs their own ESTA or visa and an e-Passport, apply early), because half our guest list is flying in and the page currently only speaks to the couple.

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'getting married in Hawaii' with Hawaii on a shortlist of destinations, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
Business details (fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale proof, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deliberately deferred and not penalised as must-fix.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, key takeaways, legal section, licence steps, timing, officiant, certificate and Australia sections and the close in full, with a skim of ESTA, permits, climate and the FAQ.
